title: A clause a decide line adds is covered by proof coverage
intention: A falsifier clause that a decide line adds is a clause proof coverage demands a tooth for, exactly as it demands one for a clause written in the falsifier field.
why: Peer F17(a) (2026-10-07): proof_coverage.clauses() reads only the falsifier field, so clause (4) of 11cd253f10bc, entered through decide line D6 ('A falsifier clause (4) is added by this line'), was invisible to lacks(). F17 ruled the falsifier is not edited to fit the gate, so 11cd's hollow had to red tooth 4 by hand, and its measured_at_build (5) records that: 'recorded by hand because proof_coverage reads only the falsifier's clauses 1-3 (F17a)'. A clause the gate cannot see is a clause that can enter PROVED with no tooth (Law 8).
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: a clause with no demanded tooth enters PROVED unproven) and Law 4 (11cd's clause (4) was covered only because the builder reddened its tooth by hand — policy where physics should be).
how: cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py: clauses(ticket) keeps its falsifier reading unchanged and appends, in decision order and without duplicates, every clause key a decision's text declares added in the form 'falsifier clause (N) is added by this line' (the phrasing of the one such line in the corpus, 11cd253f10bc D6). lacks() then names a missing PROVES key for such a clause with no other change. One new proof in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/.

proves_red.1: falsifier '(1) a (2) b (3) c' plus a decision 'A falsifier clause (4) is added by this line: d' gives clauses() == ['1','2','3','4'];
proves_red.2: lacks() over that ticket, against a fixture proof whose PROVES declares '1'-'3' only, returns a lack naming clause '4';
proves_red.3: a decision text 'D2 (6) stands; tooth (4) is green' adds nothing (clauses() == ['1','2','3']).

decisions.text: D1 THE PROOF IS ALREADY WRITTEN, AND IS NOT EDITED: cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/test_a_clause_a_decide_line_adds_is_covered.py landed at cairn e350537c with PROVES {'46ece5fd9f69': {'1','2','3'}}; against d90f5b26 teeth 1-2 FAIL and tooth 3 is ok. The build writes nothing under proofs/ — after the build, run it with bin/cairn test --exec "~/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 <that path>" and expect 3/3 green; the only file the build changes is cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py.

D2 THE BUILD, IN cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py ONLY. (a) Add a module regex beside _CLAUSE_MARK: _ADDED_CLAUSE = re.compile(r"falsifier clause \((\d{1,2})\) is added by this line", re.I) — case-INSENSITIVE, because the one corpus line (11cd253f10bc D6) opens the sentence with a capital 'A falsifier clause'. (b) The decision shape is measured on 11cd253f10bc: ticket['decisions'] is a list of dicts with keys n, text, by, step, source, at; read str text only; skip a decision that is not a dict or whose text is not a str (never raise). (c) Restructure clauses(ticket): compute the falsifier's base list EXACTLY as today (nested proves_red keys / _CLAUSE_MARK before _WRONG_INTENT / lettered run / [WHOLE] / [] for empty text), then append, in decision order, every key _ADDED_CLAUSE finds in any decision's text that is not already in the list, and return that. Every existing return path goes through the append. (d) A decision that only cites a numbered marker in prose matches nothing and adds nothing. (e) Nothing else changes: lacks(), declared(), teeth_printed() and every caller stay as they are — lacks() already reads want = clauses(ticket).
decisions.step: unlisted: modify clauses() to append decide-line clause keys from ticket['decisions']

decisions.text: D3 HOW TO RESTRUCTURE WITHOUT TOUCHING ANY RETURN PATH: rename the existing def clauses(ticket: dict) -> list[str] at proof_coverage.py:151 to def _falsifier_clauses(ticket: dict) -> list[str], leaving its body and docstring byte-for-byte unchanged (it reads the falsifier: a nested proves_red dict returns its keys; otherwise the text before WRONG-INTENT is searched for (digit) markers, then a lettered run, then [WHOLE]; empty text returns []). Then add a NEW def clauses(ticket: dict) -> list[str] directly above it: keys = _falsifier_clauses(ticket); for each d in (ticket.get('decisions') or []), if isinstance(d, dict) and isinstance(d.get('text'), str), for each k in _ADDED_CLAUSE.findall(d['text']) append k to keys when k not in keys; return keys. Give the new clauses() a short docstring naming ticket 46ece5fd9f69 and the phrase convention (open-4b3d45d375ca). No other function is renamed; every caller still calls clauses().
